title: DOINK event
description: One event as the DOINK addon records it and as the companion POSTs it to forward_url. Explained in docs/events.md. Extra fields and new event types may appear in later versions: ignore what you don't know.

seq.description: Counter per character, rising by one per recorded event, never reused. Starts again at 1 only if the addon's saved data is deleted.

ts.description: When the event happened: Unix time in seconds, from the game client's clock.

surname.description: The character's surname. Left out when the client has none.

realm.description: The realm's name as the client shows it; may contain spaces.

class.description: The class's language-independent name in capitals, e.g. WARRIOR.

level.description: The character's level when the event happened. On a level_up it is the new level.

played.description: Total time played on this character, in seconds. Present only when the player turned it on (/doink played on) and the client has answered.

group.description: Who else was in the character's party, each as "Name Surname (Class Level)". Present only when the player turned it on (/doink group on) and was in a party; left out when alone, in a raid, or when the client hid a name.

type.description: What happened; decides the shape of data.

data.description: Details of the event; the fields depend on type.

test.description: Present only on events made with /doink test. Never false.

link.description: The item link exactly as the game wrote it in chat, with its | codes.

name.description: The item's name in the player's game language.

quality.description: 0 poor, 1 common, 2 uncommon, 3 rare, 4 epic, 5 legendary.

qty.description: How many were looted at once.

vendor_value.description: What a vendor pays for the whole stack, in copper. 0 when the item can't be sold.

boe.description: Whether the item binds when equipped. null when the client didn't say.

gear.description: Whether the item is a weapon or armour. null when the client didn't say.

zone.description: The zone's name in the player's game language.

subzone.description: The area within the zone. null where the game names none.

killer.description: Who landed the last hit, from the game's death recap. null for an environmental death or when the recap was empty.

environment.description: The kind of environmental death, in capitals. null when something killed the character or the cause is unknown.

title.description: The quest's title in the player's game language; "Quest #<id>" when the client couldn't give one.

xp.description: Experience rewarded. 0 when there was none.

name.description: The encounter's name in the player's game language.

instance.description: The dungeon or raid. null when the client didn't say.

difficulty.description: The game's difficulty id for the instance.

success.description: Always true: wipes are not recorded.

group_size.description: The group size the game reports for the encounter, e.g. 5 or 40.

first_kill.description: True the first time this character kills this encounter, as far as the addon's saved data remembers.

group.description: The other party members as "Name Surname (Class Level)". null in a raid, when alone, or when the game hides the names.

skill.description: The skill's name in the player's game language.

max_rank.description: The current cap for this skill. null when the client offers none, which is always the case for weapon skills.

name.description: The mount's name in the player's game language.

item_id.description: The mount item's id, when the mount was seen as an item arriving in the bags.

spell_id.description: The mount's spell id, when the mount was seen through the mount journal.

link.description: The item link as the game wrote it, when there is an item.

bought.description: True when a vendor window was open at the time.

opponent.description: The other player's name as the game's message gave it.

fled.description: True when the duel ended because the loser left the duel area.

makgora.description: True for a Mak'gora, the duel to the death.

name.description: The battleground's name in the player's game language.
